tierRelation: E1's bound tree is the execution substrate every SQL T1 family (#1106-#1125) runs on; it landed before any of them.
E2's function catalog is what SQL T1 #1120 (42 T1 scalar functions with plan-time signature checks) registers into. Without E2 the built-ins were a frozen 10-entry table.
E3's cast registry and SqlTypeCatalog are what SQL T1 #1119 (CAST across every shared type) and #1108 (ISO multi-word type names) extend; #1422 is the remaining cast gap list.

B1-B3's typed-schema + provisioning path is where the SQL T1 DDL families land: #1121 (ON DELETE SET NULL/SET DEFAULT/NO ACTION, non-literal defaults), #1122 (ALTER TABLE RENAME, ALTER COLUMN SET/DROP DEFAULT and NOT NULL), #1123 (IDENTITY), #1124 (views).

E4's CREATE FUNCTION / CREATE DOMAIN is adjacent to but not part of T1: the plan puts triggers, procedures and user functions in T3 'a separate programmability program'. E4 delivered SQL-defined scalar functions ahead of that tier.

standaloneFollowUps.definition: Open Database items filed from reviews on this integration branch that are direct children of an area epic, not of any program's tracking issue.

fromDecision49a_B2_1355.one_liner: Bound memory in constraint validation and unique index builds: validating a constraint materializes the table's rows and a unique index build keeps every key in a set, so the deferred migration worker's memory grows with the table.
Reclaim index pages abandoned by an unpublished index build - a failed or cancelled deferred build leaves durable pages for a vacuum that does not exist yet.
An operator can repair or abandon a pending migration whose target is unreachable; today it keeps the database Degraded or offline with no administrative path out.
ALTER COLUMN changes that need a table rewrite (TYPE ... USING, scale, domain, collation); shares rewrite machinery with #1265 and relates to T1 #1122.

fromLaterReviewRounds.one_liner: DROP INDEX reclaims the index's B-tree pages; today a published index that is dropped leaks its tree until the table is dropped, so drop/recreate grows the file without bound.
Execute TIME(p)/TIMESTAMP(p)/TIMESTAMPTZ(p)/INTERVAL(p) fractional-second precision; #1438 made them fail-closed COHDBL001, so a PostgreSQL schema with TIMESTAMP(3) cannot be created.
Sdk.Database migration pipeline cannot write E4's script receipts, so Script(...) is refused in SDK projects with COHDBSDK110.
Apply the static-factory, error-message and throw-member conventions to the Database area - held back on purpose while this branch is in flight.
Report storage read failures as coded statement errors and keep the session alive.
Probe unlatched storage reads: the two-read ReadRecord path and the allocation window.
Confirm failed decodes in Graph, Documents, Blob, catalog loads and the version store (SQL and KeyValuePair done in #1362).
SQL LIKE backtracks without a bound and copies the string per step (the follow-up to #1166).
Hot-row cascades: reorder the lock queue on soft deadlocks and decide the cascade lock order.
Apply the database-name rule at declaration and in the SDK, and recover interrupted creates.

crossProgramObservations: Nothing in this branch has merged to main. 63 L03.02 items sit at 'In review', which on this board means 'landed on the integration branch', and every one of them is still OPEN on GitHub. A waterfall built from issue state alone will show them as not started.

Four of the five engine programs are effectively complete: engine extensibility (9 of 9 phases), concrete-first (8 of 9, P8 open), EventSource tracing (6 of 6 batches), storage write amplification (3 of 3 steps). Their three umbrella issues are still 'In progress' or 'Backlog'.

The programs produced 22 open follow-up items between them. Those follow-ups are children of the program issues in three cases (#1353, #1343) and children of an area epic in the rest - the inconsistency the bug-filing rule is meant to fix.

Dependency arrows that crossed program boundaries and actually gated work: #1236 -> P2 (#1258); H -> B1; B3 + P6 -> P7 (#1263); B1/B3 + E1-E3 + B2 + P7 -> tracing batch D (#1349). A roadmap that draws programs as independent swimlanes will be wrong about all four.

The Hardening epic #1511 is one day old and already the second-largest Database epic by item count (37). It carries its own Priority/Wave/Effort model inside the feature bodies, which the project board's own Priority and Wave fields do not yet reflect.

openOwnerSignOffs.one_liner: ON DELETE CASCADE has no depth limit (PostgreSQL's model); the proposed guard is a statement and lock timeout (#1231), not a level count.
COHSQLE005/006, COHDBG007/008/009 treated as accepted unless the owner objects.
Should outside ISqlDatabaseEngineBuilder implementations reach AddSql and application composition, or only standalone composition?
A writer whose undo fails keeps its locks until the purge pass - in Graph, Documents and Blob that blocks every writer.
Reclamation owner, a database-wide reader fence, and DROP of a populated table - implemented as recommended, owner to confirm.
VARCHAR/CHAR/binary length cap at 10,485,760 and refusing temporal precision qualifiers as COHDBL001 - owner to confirm (#1509 is the follow-up that undoes the second half).
DatabaseType.Character as a new shared enum member and a per-column max length in the SQL result header at format 2 - owner to confirm.
Whether index pages keep physical rollback at all (a written comparison is the deliverable).
Adding a Code property to the area-root DatabaseException (public API in the root).
